feijao2019.title: Report of the Expert Panel on the Technical Causes of the Failure of Feijão Dam I

polley2015.authors: Independent Expert Engineering Investigation and Review Panel
polley2015.title: Report on Mount Polley Tailings Storage Facility Breach

polley-cim2015.title: Mount Polley Mine Tailings Storage Facility Breach, August 4, 2014: Investigation Report of the Chief Inspector of Mines
polley-cim2015.container: BC Ministry of Energy and Mines, 30 November 2015

luino2012.title: The Stava mudflow of 19 July 1985 (Northern Italy): a disaster that effective regulation might have prevented
luino2012.container: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences 12: 1029–1044
luino2012.note: Abstract: the upper dam burst on 19 July 1985, the mudflow (180,000 m³) ran more than 4.2 km, 268 died; foremost among the causes, the mistaken assumption that the tailings would consolidate fairly quickly. The text describes the upper basin as raised by the upstream method and the mud pouring from the upper into the lower impoundment.

foster2000.authors: Foster, M., Fell, R., Spannagle, M.
foster2000.title: The statistics of embankment dam failures and accidents

gistm2020.authors: International Council on Mining and Metals, United Nations Environment Programme and Principles for Responsible Investment
gistm2020.title: Global Industry Standard on Tailings Management

oroville2018.title: Independent Forensic Team Report: Oroville Dam Spillway Incident

bchydro-cbrac2016.title: Virtual tour of Revelstoke and Mica
bchydro-cbrac2016.container: Presentation to the Columbia Basin Regional Advisory Committee, October 2016
bchydro-cbrac2016.note: Revelstoke's concrete dam: 470 m long, 126 m thick at the base, 9 m at the crest; it 'relies on its massive weight and resultant friction to hold back the reservoir'.

franks2021.authors: Franks, D.M., Stringer, M., Torres-Cruz, L.A., Baker, E., Valenta, R., Thygesen, K., Matthews, A., Howchin, J., Barrie, S.
franks2021.title: Tailings facility disclosures reveal stability risks
franks2021.note: p. 1: Brumadinho, 259 deaths and a further 11 people missing; the investors' disclosure request of 5 April 2019, answered by 107 companies. pp. 1–2: 1,743 facilities, 44.5 billion m³ stored, 750 m deep over Manhattan; about 2.5 billion m³ a year expected for 2019–2023.

fourie2001.authors: Fourie, A.B., Blight, G.E., Papageorgiou, G.
fourie2001.title: Static liquefaction as a possible explanation for the Merriespruit tailings dam failure
fourie2001.note: p. 707 (abstract): 17 deaths; insufficient freeboard provision and often poor pool control; overtopping and erosion exposed metastable tailings, which liquefied. p. 708: a 31 m gold tailings dam, February 1994, about 50 mm of rain, about 600,000 m³ flowed about 3 km; upstream (daywall paddock) construction; water flowed over the crest for 1 to 2 hours.

fundao2016.authors: Fundão Tailings Dam Review Panel: Morgenstern, N.R. (chair), Vick, S.G., Viotti, C.B., Watts, B.D.
fundao2016.title: Report on the Immediate Causes of the Failure of the Fundão Dam
fundao2016.note: p. i: a liquefaction flowslide on 5 November 2015, beginning at the left abutment; the dam was raised by the upstream method. p. ii: three small seismic shocks about 90 minutes earlier likely accelerated a failure already well advanced. p. 18: 32 million m³ of tailings lost, 61% of the contents.

stava-elcobre.title: The El Cobre tailings dam failure, 1965
stava-elcobre.note: 28 March 1965, a copper mine in the El Cobre district, Chile; a dyke built by upstream hydraulic filling, 35 m high; set off by an earthquake and ascribed to liquefaction; 1.9 million m³ of 4.25 million m³ stored ran 12 km; over 200 deaths. Its own sources: Dobry and Alvarez (1967) and the WISE chronology.

stava-fundao.title: The Fundão tailings dams failure, 2015
stava-fundao.note: 17 confirmed deaths and two people missing; a mudflow of more than 30 million m³; over 660 km down three rivers to the Atlantic.

adamo2020.authors: Adamo, N., Al-Ansari, N., Sissakian, V., Laue, J., Knutsson, S.
adamo2020.title: Dam safety problems related to seepage
adamo2020.container: Journal of Earth Sciences and Geotechnical Engineering 10(6): 191–239
adamo2020.note: pp. 194–195 and Table 1: Foster, Fell and Spannagle's statistics of large embankment dam failures to 1986, from a database of 11,192 dams; 136 failures in all, 124 in operation, with the counts and shares by mode.

bc-dsr2016.title: Dam Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 40/2016
bc-dsr2016.container: Under the Water Sustainability Act; deposited and effective 29 February 2016
bc-dsr2016.note: Applies to dams that store or divert water; dams under 7.5 m high holding no more than 10,000 m³ are excluded unless ordered otherwise.

bc-hsrc-part10.authors: British Columbia, Ministry of Mining and Critical Minerals
bc-hsrc-part10.title: Health, Safety and Reclamation Code for Mines in British Columbia, Part 10: Permitting, Reclamation and Closure
bc-hsrc-part10.note: Section 10.4.1: an engineer of record for each tailings storage facility and dam. Section 10.4.3: an Independent Tailings Review Board for a mine with one or more tailings storage facilities, unless the chief inspector exempts it.

cda2019-mining.title: Technical Bulletin: Application of Dam Safety Guidelines to Mining Dams
cda2019-mining.note: Complements the 2013 Dam Safety Guidelines with how they apply to mining dams, many of which must function indefinitely.

bchydro-peace2020.title: Peace River System Dam Safety: BC Hydro Projects Update
bchydro-peace2020.note: W.A.C. Bennett Dam is an earthfill embankment dam, 2,040 m across the top, 183 m high and 800 m thick at its base.
